LHX.sentence: L3Harris is down slightly, and the real issue is that it earns a thinner profit on each dollar of work than the bigger defense companies do — that gap is why the stock has lagged, even though military spending itself is steady.

ASML.sentence: ASML ticked up a touch after a pullback from its high, and nothing's wrong with the business — they're still the only company in the world that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is basically flat and doing its usual quiet thing — selling industrial gases under long contracts and nudging prices up, which makes it the kind of steady name investors lean on when the broader market gets shaky.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quietly outpacing the other big tech names heading into earnings, with its cloud-and-AI story grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher dipped a bit, but biotech funding is thawing again, and more money flowing to labs usually shows up in their orders a few quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady — it runs oil and gas pipelines like a toll road and pays a generous dividend, which looks fairly priced right now rather than a bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has been one of the strongest performers in its software group even while sitting well below its peak, as big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI automation tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore fell nearly 3% and has been lagging the recent surge in copper prices, which is odd given how much copper it mines — the gap between the two is the thing worth watching.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta eased off, but the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still rising at a healthy clip — the headline number looks weaker only because of the mix of products sold, not any real softening.

KOF.sentence: The Mexican Coca-Cola bottler is fine on the ground, but a weakening Mexican peso shrinks its earnings once they're converted into dollars, which is the main thing weighing on it.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a good day as oil prices stay high above the cost of pumping it, which keeps its big dividend well-funded — though oil has run up a lot lately.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, dropped nearly 4% and is now priced below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — the kind of cheap level that often marks the bottom of a shipping cycle.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped and is unusually trading at a slight discount to its twin Visa, even though people keep tapping their cards more than ever — so this is a pricing quirk, not a business problem.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company jumped 3% and sits well off its high, but hospitals are still expected to do more operations with its machines next year, so the fear baked into the price isn't showing up in the actual business.
